analysis: Reviewed the docs/architecture/inference.md head text (lines 404-1204) and the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.swift patch. The Swift change adds an enum case `missingUserQuery` with a static, content-free message ('This model requires at least one user message that is not only a tool response'). It carries no request content, so it adds no consumer-prompt disclosure (A-001, T-008). The doc says this case maps to typed HTTP 400 instead of 500 `template_render`, validated by `Qwen35TemplateFixes.validateUserQuery`. That mapping lives in `ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift` and `Qwen35TemplateFixes.swift`, which were not supplied. A next pass should confirm the new case is handled in every exhaustive switch and that the sanitized mapping does not leak history. The doc changes are descriptive only, covering the MTP idle upgrade drain, typical acceptance, Bonsai 9B policy, MiMo, and Qwen4 admission. They change no security controls. The prefix-cache statements (T-041) say sampler settings are not part of cache identity, and that SSD caching is enabled by default for the Bonsai 9B identities with existing identity and security checks. That is consistent with the T-041 mitigations. The MTP idle-upgrade drain uses 503 `slot_state` and keeps other models available, which touches availability (T-010, T-029), but no code change is supplied to evaluate. Coverage limit: the doc claims about code behavior (e.g. `beginDrain`, `commitIfIdle`, typical acceptance) could not be verified against source.
